at_rest.defends_against: a file-read-only primitive held by the non-root `git` account (a path traversal in the transport wrapper, say), for the two 0600 files. Also closes the /proc/<pid>/cmdline channel for both credentials: every POST passes its header via `curl -K -` on stdin, and both redactors read their sed script from a 0600 file rather than an -e operand, so no external process carries a secret in argv (cmdline is mode 444; environ is 400). ALSO, since #7772: CODE EXECUTION as a NON-ROOT account can no longer read user_data from the Hetzner metadata endpoint. A host-local nftables rule (write_files /usr/local/bin/git-data-nftables.sh + git-data-nftables.service, armed by a runcmd `systemctl enable --now`) drops 169.254.169.254 for `meta skuid != 0`. Measured at #7772 on the prior host image (Ubuntu 24.04 / nftables v1.0.9); not re-measured after the 2026-10-11 rebirth: root still reaches the endpoint, non-root is dropped, and an un-ruled control address still reaches. Root is exempt so cloud-init's own datasource is unaffected.
at_rest.does_not_defend: CODE EXECUTION AS ROOT, which reads user_data from the metadata endpoint exactly as before — the #7772 nftables drop is scoped to non-root UIDs by design (ADR-198's own wording), so it narrows this from 'any account' to 'root only'. Also does not defend the 0755 sentry_dsn copy, which the `git` account can read today, nor a FILE-READ primitive against /etc/default/git-data-doppler by anything that can read root-owned 0600 files. Rotation of the baked ingest token still requires a host replace (user_data is ForceNew, ADR-149/ADR-152). Closed predecessor tracker: #7772; the baked token that can fetch GIT_DATA_LUKS_KEY is listed for the git-data host in #8620
at_rest.live_verification: unavailable:the git-data host was reborn 2026-10-11 (Hetzner API read 2026-10-12: server 169724272, created 2026-10-11T12:50:15Z, rotate run 38140050880; earlier births 2026-09-14 runs 34836141887 and 34861860722); no on-host posture probe exists; related #6167

exception.justification: credentials baked into user_data are plaintext by construction - user_data is retrievable from the Hetzner metadata endpoint BY ROOT, so no on-host file mode can make them encrypted-at-rest. The two 0600 files bound a file-read-only primitive; the 0755 sentry_dsn copy predates #7460 and is bounded by nothing. Accepted on the ADR-198 capability test: every credential here has a write-only ingest ceiling. GIT_DATA_LUKS_KEY fails that test and is deliberately NOT baked. #7772 closed legs (2) and (3) of that test for the ingest token specifically - per-source isolation and the non-root metadata drop - so what remains accepted here is narrower than when this row was written.
exception.reevaluate_when: the next git-data host rebuild window, or 2026-12-31, whichever is first. The 2026-10-11 rebirth (rotate run 38140050880) did not close the residual leg: the baked doppler_token can still derive GIT_DATA_LUKS_KEY. #8620 tracks that token's presence on the root disk; the root read of user_data from the metadata endpoint is not closed by encrypting the root disk, so closing #8620 alone does not retire this row.

in_transit.does_not_defend: a leaked anon/service key; TLS protects the channel, not the credential

connections.enforced_at: apps/web-platform/infra/zot-registry.tf / model.c4 (edge: hetzner -> zotRegistry "Pulls app image")

in_transit.tls: none (plain HTTP on the private network by design)
in_transit.does_not_defend: a passive on-net attacker could read pulled image bytes AND the zot pull credential (HTTP Basic on every login/pull; read-only per cloud-init-registry.yml accessControl actions [read]; the same random_password.zot_pull the inngest host bakes, and since #8651 also baked into every fresh web host's user_data); integrity (not confidentiality) comes from the @sha256 digest pin (docker verifies content against it) on every pull, plus the cosign signature check on the deploy path only; a fresh web boot runs no signature check, which is why it sends ONLY @sha256-pinned refs to zot

exception.justification: private-network-only registry link; integrity comes from @sha256 digest pinning (plus cosign verification on the deploy path), not TLS; the image bytes are NOT public (the GHCR package is private), so confidentiality on this link rests on the private network alone. Compensating control, as recorded for this link and not re-measured 2026-10-12: it is carried on the Hetzner private network (the separate CI path through the CF Tunnel has its own row); the nftables peer restrictions on the registry were not re-read for this renewal. Renewed to 2026-11-12 pending the CLO ruling due 2026-10-24. The published unqualified TLS sentence (privacy-policy.md / data-protection-disclosure.md, 2026-09-28) is referred to the 2026-10-24 CLO ruling and disclosed_as stays not-publicly-claimed pending it (#10136).
exception.reevaluate_when: the registry is exposed beyond the private network, a new tenant joins 10.0.1.0/24, or TLS is added to the link

connections.connection: GitHub Actions runner -> Better Stack Logs INGEST (s2457081.eu-fsn-3.betterstackdata.com)
connections.enforced_at: scripts/zot-inventory.sh (the SOLEUR_ZOT_INVENTORY POST); URL pinned at apps/web-platform/infra/zot-registry.tf local.betterstack_logs_ingest_url

in_transit.does_not_defend: a leaked BETTERSTACK_LOGS_TOKEN (ingest-only: it can write log lines, it cannot read them); TLS protects the channel, not the credential. Also does not defend against a CI POST bypassing Vector's VRL PII scrub - every host emitter reaches this source through a Vector agent that redacts and a runner curl does not - mitigated by construction (the marker carries only counts, sizes, our own OCI repo names and digests) and asserted by a field allow-list test derived from the construction site.

connections.connection: GitHub Actions runner -> zot registry over the CF Tunnel (registry.<base> -> tcp://10.0.1.30:5000)

in_transit.tls: runner<->CF edge and CF edge<->origin connector: TLS 1.2+ (raw TCP over WebSocket). origin connector<->10.0.1.30:5000: PLAIN HTTP on the Hetzner private network, by design.
in_transit.does_not_defend: a passive on-net attacker on 10.0.1.0/24 could read image bytes on the final leg; integrity comes from cosign digest-pinning, not TLS. Also does not defend a leaked CF Access service token or a leaked zot pull credential.

exception.justification: the same private-network-only exception already recorded for 'web hosts -> zot registry' - the final leg is plain HTTP inside the Hetzner private network; image bytes are our own OCI layers and integrity is cosign-digest-pinned. Folded in here rather than deferred because #7278 adds the fifth CI caller to this leg. Compensating control, as recorded for this link and not re-measured 2026-10-12: the runner-to-edge and edge-to-connector legs are TLS 1.2+ and only the final leg is plain HTTP on the private network; the nftables peer restrictions were not re-read for this renewal. Renewed to 2026-11-12 pending the CLO ruling due 2026-10-24. The published unqualified TLS sentence (privacy-policy.md / data-protection-disclosure.md, 2026-09-28) is referred to the 2026-10-24 CLO ruling and disclosed_as stays not-publicly-claimed pending it (#10136).
exception.reevaluate_when: the registry link gains TLS, a new tenant joins 10.0.1.0/24, or the store is exposed beyond the private network

connections.connection: web-platform app (web hosts) <-> dedicated inngest host (10.0.1.40:8288, and its sdk_url call-back to 10.0.1.10:3000/api/inngest)

in_transit.tls: none (plain HTTP on the Hetzner private network by design, ADR-100)
in_transit.does_not_defend: a passive on-net attacker on 10.0.1.0/24 could read INNGEST_EVENT_KEY (in the /e/<key> send path), the hashed signing key (Bearer signkey-prod-<sha256>), event payloads and step outputs; replaying a sniffed key additionally requires sending from a web host's private IP (the inngest host's nftables allows :8288 only from 10.0.1.10/10.0.1.11). The raw signing key never crosses the wire (Inngest->app requests carry only an HMAC).

exception.justification: the same private-network-only plaintext exception recorded for the zot registry link: the app<->scheduler channel stays inside the Hetzner private network, both ends were recorded as nftables-restricted to the web hosts' private IPs, and the peers on 10.0.1.0/24 are our own hosts (git-data .20, registry .30). Transport confidentiality on this link is accepted, not provided; recorded when the #6178 2.4 app-repoint (#8191) moved the channel off the host loopback. Renewed to 2026-11-12 pending the CLO ruling due 2026-10-24; this hop carries event payloads and step outputs, so it is the priority link to close. Not re-measured 2026-10-12: nftables peer restrictions. The published unqualified TLS sentence (privacy-policy.md / data-protection-disclosure.md, 2026-09-28) is referred to the 2026-10-24 CLO ruling and disclosed_as stays not-publicly-claimed pending it (#10136).
exception.reevaluate_when: the channel gains TLS, a non-Jikigai peer joins 10.0.1.0/24, a new tenant joins 10.0.1.0/24, or the inngest host is reachable beyond the private network

connections.connection: GitHub Actions runner -> web-1 sshd (bash callers of the CF tunnel SSH bridge, via cloudflared access tcp)
connections.enforced_at: .github/actions/cf-tunnel-ssh-bridge/action.yml step 'Decode CI SSH private key (TF_VAR + optional keyfile/WEB_HOST_SSH export)' (WEB_HOST_SSH: StrictHostKeyChecking=yes, HostKeyAlias=web-1, HostKeyAlgorithms=ecdsa-sha2-nistp256) + .github/actions/cf-tunnel-ssh-bridge/write-known-hosts.sh; pin: apps/web-platform/infra/web-1-ssh-host-key.pub (ADR-237)

in_transit.tls: SSH-2 inside a Cloudflare-verified TLS tunnel (runner<->CF edge<->origin connector); web-1 authenticated by its committed ECDSA-P256 host key
in_transit.does_not_defend: a compromised web-1 (it holds the real host key); a stolen CI SSH key plus a CF Access service token (that authenticates as CI, not as the host); a wrong committed pin is caught only by the pre-merge and merge-time probes, not by this connection

connections.connection: GitHub Actions runner / operator -> web-1 sshd (Terraform connection blocks through the same bridge)
connections.enforced_at: apps/web-platform/infra/server.tf locals web_1_ssh_host_key + host_key in every connection block (server.tf, ci-ssh-key.tf); terraform_data.web_1_host_key_probe re-runs on a pin or terraform_version change

in_transit.tls: SSH-2 (Terraform's Go crypto/ssh client), web-1 authenticated by its committed ECDSA-P256 host key
in_transit.does_not_defend: a compromised web-1 (it holds the real host key); a stolen CI SSH key plus a CF Access service token; an operator-local apply that edits the pin file to whatever it observes

connections.connection: GitHub Actions runner -> git-data sshd (direct-tcpip through web-1, git-data-cutover.yml)
connections.enforced_at: .github/workflows/git-data-cutover.yml step 'Write git-data ssh_config' (Host 10.0.1.10 and Host 10.0.1.20: StrictHostKeyChecking yes, HostKeyAlias web-1 / git-data) + apps/web-platform/infra/git-data-flag-precheck.sh (GIT_DATA_SSH_HOST_KEY read, fails closed when absent)

in_transit.tls: SSH-2 end to end runner<->git-data (ED25519 host key, Terraform-minted and rotated on every replace), nested inside the pinned web-1 session
in_transit.does_not_defend: a reader of main-root Terraform state (which holds the host private key, also embedded in git-data's user_data) who also holds a network position (#8209); a rooted git-data host answering falsely (a pinned key authenticates the host, not its answers)

connections.connection: web-1 app container -> git-data sshd (Hetzner private network, 10.0.1.20:22)

in_transit.tls: SSH-2 over the Hetzner private network; git-data authenticated by its Terraform-minted ED25519 host key (GIT_DATA_SSH_HOST_KEY), pinned on every dial; an absent or malformed pin refuses. Unpinned fallback arm deleted by PR #9096, #5914; ADR-237 Addendum
in_transit.does_not_defend: a reader of main-root Terraform state (the host private key lives there and in user_data) who also holds a private-network position (#8209); a writer of Doppler prd who replaces GIT_DATA_SSH_HOST_KEY with their own key and holds a private-network position (the app then pins the impersonator; detected only after the fact by scheduled-terraform-drift.yml); a rooted web-1, which holds the transport, provision and remove keys; a rooted git-data answering falsely under its own key
